text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 1.6% today and is down 2.5% over two weeks, tracking a sharp drop from $412.85 on November 12th to $367.93 today. The main pressure appears to be geopolitical: news of Iranian military attacks on U.S. positions in Kuwait and broader instability in the Strait of Hormuz have created uncertainty in Middle Eastern oil flows, while simultaneously the IEA warned that confidence in the region as a reliable energy corridor has collapsed. Paradoxically, while these tensions typically tighten oil supplies and benefit refiners, U.S. crude is trading at $89.53 per barrel—down noticeably from recent highs—suggesting markets are pricing in either demand concerns or expectations that disruption risk is already priced in.

The backdrop also includes softer near-term refinery economics: U.S. refineries are running at 95.7% capacity (high utilization), but gasoline and diesel inventories remain elevated, which can compress the margins refiners earn per barrel processed. Meanwhile, longer-term permitting reform (the BAAJA bill) passed the Senate and could ease future energy development, but that's a gradual tailwind, not an immediate earnings driver.
